items.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: INTERVIEWER mentions 'Whelman and Broad' as people who contributed to the language; INTERVIEWEE responds by naming 'Walter Wright' but does not mention Whelman or describe a personal relationship with him.

ctx.x: So on the bass when… you talked about the tuba and the fact that they played the Arco on the bass, and you talked about Whelman and Broad, were there others who really contributed to the language, a lot to the language that you used in Chicago so that you‟d say well hey, this is the way to play properly in this style, this is the way we do it. Were there people that you looked up to?

Yeah. Walter Wright, very wonderful bassist, a New Orleans… tall, dignified, a no frills guy. Sometimes the no frills guy didn‟t get through because he didn‟t take a partying and all that kind of stuff.
